channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: De Lula a Flávio: veja os candidatos que mais moveram ações na Justiça
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro leads among presidential candidates in the number of lawsuits filed, with 11 cases in the Federal District, mostly involving moral damages and image rights. Other candidates like Ronaldo Caiado and Renan Santos also have multiple lawsuits, while Lula has five image rights cases. Despite some victories, Flávio lost recent lawsuits against federal deputy Rogério Correia and a retiree, with claims for compensation and public retraction denied.

item.title: Quem é Vera Lúcia, candidata do PSTU ao governo de São Paulo
item.description: Vera Lúcia, a trade unionist and former shoemaker worker from Pernambuco, is the PSTU's candidate for governor of São Paulo in 2026, with Renata França as her running mate. She has decades of experience in the labor movement and has previously run for mayor of Aracaju (four times), federal deputy from Sergipe (2006 and 2014), mayor of São Paulo (2020), and president of Brazil (2018 and 2022), without being elected in any of those attempts.

item.title: Quem é Carlos Machado, candidato do PCB ao governo de São Paulo
item.description: Carlos Machado, a historian and public school teacher from Franca, is the Brazilian Communist Party (PCB) candidate for governor of São Paulo. His campaign centers on socialism, ending capitalist exploitation, and fighting racism, sexism, femicide, and LGBTphobia, while opposing privatizations and advocating for the re-estatization of São Paulo. His running mate is Felipe de Oliveira Queiroz.

item.title: Quem é Izadora Dias, candidata do PCO ao governo de São Paulo
item.description: Izadora Dias, 31, is the Partido da Causa Operária (PCO) candidate for governor of São Paulo in the 2026 elections. A militant since 2018, she is a Letters student at USP, former coordinator of the João Cândido collective and current coordinator of the Rosa Luxemburgo women's collective. In 2022, she ran for federal deputy under the PCO and received 237 votes; current polls show her with 0.1% voting intention.

item.title: Favorito, Tarcísio inicia campanha em busca de votos da Grande SP
item.description: Tarcísio de Freitas launched his re-election campaign in Osasco, a key city in Greater São Paulo where he narrowly lost to Fernando Haddad in 2022. The strategy focuses on winning the metropolitan region, seen as crucial for securing a first-round victory, with support from allies like Ricardo Nunes and participation in events featuring national right-wing figures. Winning Greater São Paulo could be decisive for repeating a first-round win, a feat not achieved in the state since 2014.

item.title: Haddad busca combater antipetismo em campanha pelo governo de SP
item.description: Fernando Haddad (PT) is running for governor of São Paulo for the second time in 2026, after losing the runoff to Tarcísio de Freitas in 2022. His campaign faces high PT rejection, especially in the interior, with 47% disapproval in a July Datafolha poll, compared to Tarcísio’s 29%. To counter antipetism, Haddad emphasizes everyday policy proposals and selected Márcio França (PSB) as his running mate, while holding the party convention in Campinas to appeal to interior voters.

item.title: Vice de Flávio empregou vice-prefeita de cidade onde emenda Pix sumiu
item.description: Alfredo Gaspar (PL-AL), running mate of Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), employed Ravena Caldeira de Araújo (MDB), the current vice-mayor of São José da Laje, as a parliamentary secretary from February 2023 to July 2024. During this time, Gaspar allocated a R$ 6.2 million Pix amendment to the municipality, which subsequently vanished from the city’s account. Gaspar’s office denied any wrongdoing, stating the hires of Ravena and her husband were lawful and occurred at separate times.

item.title: Inter recebe o Remo em duelo direto contra o Z4 do Brasileirão
item.description: Internacional and Remo face off in a direct clash to avoid relegation in the Brasileirão, with Inter in 17th place (23 points) and Remo just below in 18th (22 points). The match takes place this Monday (August 17) at 8:00 PM at Beira-Rio, where Inter holds a strong historical advantage, having won all three home encounters. Inter arrives with inconsistent form, while Remo seeks to escape the relegation zone after mixed results in recent games.

item.title: “Janja terá papel fundamental na campanha, gostem ou não”, diz neta de Lula
item.description: Bia Lula, a president’s granddaughter and a communications expert, stated that First Lady Janja will play a fundamental role in Lula’s 2026 re-election campaign, praising her active and unconventional approach that defied traditional first-lady expectations. She added that Janja was crucial in keeping Lula motivated during the 2022 campaign and has visibly revitalized his appearance and energy since. The remarks were made at the campaign launch event in São Bernardo do Campo, São Paulo.

item.title: Veja a agenda dos candidatos ao governo de Minas nesta segunda (17/8)
item.description: On Monday (17/8), Flávio Roscoe (PL) holds events in Juiz de Fora alongside Flávio Bolsonaro, including a motorcycle rally and political rally in the morning, followed by the launch of his Minas Gerais gubernatorial campaign at night in Belo Horizonte. Mateus Simões (PSD) also has schedules in BH and Araxá. Flávio Bolsonaro's visit to Juiz de Fora symbolizes the 2018 stabbing attack on his father, Jair Bolsonaro, and comes two days after a search warrant was issued against a man who made online threats.

item.title: Neta de Lula diz ter pretensão política, mas afirma que respeitará a lei
item.description: Bia Lula, granddaughter of Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, said she has political aspirations for the future but emphasized she will respect electoral law, which bars relatives up to the third degree of a head of state from running for public office while the relative is in power. She currently coordinates a state deputy’s campaign in Rio de Janeiro and is building her political path through study and dialogue, especially with her grandfather, on issues like gender-based violence and women’s safety.

item.title: PF acha mensagens de Lulinha falando de negócios com lobista do Careca do INSS: "Nosso futuro é Suíça"
item.description: The Federal Police found messages from Fábio Luís da Silva, known as Lulinha, son of President Lula, discussing business with lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger, who is under investigation for influence peddling. The conversations show Lulinha participated in meetings with key government figures, including Marcola (former chief of staff) and Berger (former Health Ministry executive), and Roberta stated 'our future is Switzerland'. There are indications Lulinha received payments linked to the 'Careca do INSS', a lobbyist suspected of trying to sell medicinal cannabis to the SUS.

item.title: PL é o partido mais branco e tem menos mulheres candidatas que a média
item.description: The PL has the lowest share of Black candidates (6.3% Black) and the highest share of white candidates (61.0%) above the national average, along with only 33.0% female candidates — below the national average of 34.8%. The party of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro also lags in Black representation, while the PCB leads with 65.2% Black candidates, albeit with very few total candidates. The data underscores Flávio Bolsonaro’s challenges in appealing to majority demographics — women (51.5% of Brazilians) and Black people (55.5%) — despite efforts to include women in his presidential ticket.

item.title: O voto da maioria: o que pensa e o que quer o eleitor da Classe C - O Assunto #1784
item.description: The C Class, representing over half of Brazilian voters with a monthly per capita family income between R$ 610 and R$ 1.250, is portrayed as a heterogeneous, less ideological and more pragmatic group whose vote will be decisive in the 2026 election. According to Renato Meirelles, author of 'Brazil of the Majority', this electorate holds specific views on the state, labor market, entrepreneurship, and cultural and religious values, and responds best to political figures who communicate effectively with their daily reality.

item.title: Colidio e Sosa têm estreia pelo Vasco frustrada em derrota marcada por 'apagão' diante do Santos; análise
item.description: Vasco lost 3-0 to Santos at São Januário, with goals from Gabigol, Willian Arão, and Luan Peres, pushing the club into the relegation zone. The debuts of Argentine signings Sosa and Colidio were disappointing, as both struggled to influence the game and missed clear chances. The crowd booed president Pedrinho, the team, and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, who attended the match and was greeted before kickoff.

item.title: 'Sósia' de Alexandre de Moraes circula entre vips em comício de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: A lookalike of Alexandre de Moraes, Julio Sergio Carneiro Marques (Julinho Dborais), attended the launch of Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential campaign in Rio, wearing a judge's robe and tie but no pants, instead using a diaper and carrying a toilet seat with Lula's photo. He was approached by Bolsonaro supporters, took selfies, and spoke with right-wing figures like Senator Rogério Marinho. Julinho is a federal deputy candidate for Partido Novo and previously ran for city council under the PT in 2004.

item.title: Flávio, Caiado e Renan usam colete à prova de balas em primeiro dia de campanha; Lula e Zema dispensam equipamento
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, Ronaldo Caiado, and Renan Santos began their presidential campaigns wearing bulletproof vests, while Lula and Romeu Zema chose not to use the equipment. These choices reflect differing security strategies and campaign messaging, with Flávio and Caiado emphasizing public safety and Lula and Zema opting for a more open, less militarized approach. The agendas included street events, walks, and rallies, marking the official start of the electoral race.

item.title: Pretos e pardos representam 49,9% das candidaturas registradas para as eleições de 2026
item.description: Black and mixed-race candidates account for 49.9% of the 20,496 candidacies registered for the 2026 elections, according to the TSE, with 10,224 registrations — a slight decrease from 50.3% in 2022. Participation varies by office: 23.1% for president, 40.5% for state governors, and 37.1% for Senate. Pardos represent 36.3% and pretos 13.6%, while white candidates make up 48.7%.

item.title: Lula volta a mencionar mágoa com Toffoli e reforça distância na relação com ministro do STF desde a crise Vorcaro
item.description: Lula again criticized STF Minister Dias Toffoli for blocking his attendance at his brother Vavá's funeral in 2019 while he was imprisoned during Operation Lava-Jato. He contrasted this with the permission he received during the military dictatorship to bury his mother, arguing that character, not era, defines a person. Lula emphasized that Toffoli was his own appointee to the Court, underscoring the personal grievance and ongoing estrangement.

item.title: Lula visita operação da Petrobras na Margem Equatorial após descoberta de petróleo
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva visits a Petrobras drillship in the Equatorial Margin off the coast of Amapá on Monday, following the state oil company's announcement of oil and gas indications in the Morpho well in the Foz do Amazonas Basin. The visit, three days after the discovery announcement, underscores Petrobras' strategy to bolster reserves and national energy security amid potential future decline in pre-salt production. Exploration in the Equatorial Margin, stretching from Amapá to Rio Grande do Norte, remains contingent on further environmental approvals and has sparked debate over potential ecological impacts.

item.title: Lobista ligada a Lulinha comprou joias para Marcola, diz jornal
item.description: The Federal Police discovered that lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger purchased jewelry worth R$9,200 for Marco Aurélio Ribeiro, former Chief of Staff to President Lula, known as Marcola, at his request, for Mother's Day 2024. The purchase is linked to an investigation into alleged influence-peddling involving Lulinha, the president's son, and lobbyist 'Careca do INSS'. The defense of Luchsinger and Marcola did not respond to inquiries by publication time.

item.title: PT diz que ato de Lula teve 40.000 pessoas
item.description: The PT claimed 40,000 attendees at Lula’s campaign launch in São Bernardo do Campo, near the stadium’s total capacity of 41,138, exceeding its initial expectation of 20,000. The party said the field was used to accommodate extra attendees but did not disclose its counting methodology, and drone restrictions prevented independent verification. Such discrepancies between organizer estimates and static capacity are common in political events.

item.title: Ato de Flávio em Copacabana reúne 8,9 mil pessoas, diz monitor da USP
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's rally in Copacabana drew 8,900 people at its peak, according to USP/Cebrap monitoring, falling short of previous right-wing rallies led by his father, Jair Bolsonaro, in the same location. The estimate, with a 12% margin of error, ranges from 7,800 to 9,900 participants, using AI-based crowd counting methodology.

item.title: Assista ao vídeo e leia o discurso de Lula no estádio 1º de Maio
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva launched his 2026 re-election campaign at a rally in the Estádio 1º de Maio in São Bernardo do Campo, a symbolic site of his union activism in the 1970s and 1980s. In a 36-minute speech, Lula recalled his working-class roots, discussed his health following skin cancer treatment, and paid tribute to deceased intellectuals and comrades, reinforcing his bond with the PT’s grassroots base.

item.title: Autoridade do governo Trump acusa Brasil de censura após X adotar filtro para eleição
item.description: Sarah B. Rogers, U.S. Undersecretary of State for Public Diplomacy, accused Brazil of imposing censorship after X (formerly Twitter) adjusted its algorithm to comply with Brazil's 2026 electoral rules. The claim emerged amid diplomatic tensions over content moderation and elections in Brazil.

item.title: Número de candidaturas com nomes religiosos cai e é o menor desde 2010
item.description: The number of candidates using religious references in their ballot names dropped 40% in 2024 compared to the 2022 elections, according to a UOL survey based on TSE data. This represents the lowest figure since 2010, signaling a declining trend in the use of religious elements for electoral identification. The analysis covers all candidacies registered in this year's election.

item.title: Candidatos declaram R$ 116,7 milhões em aeronaves nas eleições de 2026
item.description: Candidates in the 2026 elections declared 78 aircraft-related assets to the TSE, totaling over R$116.7 million, including jets, airplanes, helicopters, fractional ownerships, and acquisition rights. The disclosure highlights substantial private aviation wealth among electoral contenders.

item.title: Evento de Lula autoriza uso de imagem e voz sem remuneração
item.description: Lula launched his re-election campaign in São Bernardo do Campo with a notice authorizing free use of participants' image and voice, without compensation. The event, held at the historic Estádio 1º de Maio, reinforced his union roots and launched the slogan 'Brazil ready for more'. Lula highlighted priorities such as national defense, rare earth exploration, and full-time education, amid tensions with the United States.

item.title: Campanha rumo ao Planalto começa com atos públicos nos redutos dos candidatos
item.description: The official 2026 election campaign kicked off on Sunday with public events by Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro in symbolic strongholds. Lula, speaking in São Bernardo do Campo, emphasized national sovereignty, combating violence against women, rare earth exploitation, and organized crime, while Flávio Bolsonaro, in Copacabana, framed himself as the continuation of his father’s political project, promising to appoint STF justices 'against abortion, against drugs' who would not persecute political opponents. Other candidates, including Renan Santos (Missão), also held events to mark the campaign’s start.

item.title: Autoridade do governo Trump acusa Brasil de censura após mudança no algoritmo do X para eleições
item.description: U.S. Deputy Secretary of State Sarah B. Rogers accused Brazil of censorship after X (formerly Twitter) updated its algorithm to comply with Brazil’s TSE Resolution No. 23.610/2019, which excludes official candidate profiles from organic recommendations unless paid promotion is used. The change aligns the platform with Brazil’s 2026 electoral rules, without removing content or accounts. The criticism comes amid rising diplomatic tensions between the Trump and Lula governments over digital regulation, trade, and freedom of expression, including reported U.S. considerations of sanctions against Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes.

item.title: Ato de Flávio em Copacabana reúne 8,9 mil pessoas no Rio, estima USP
item.description: The first campaign rally of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) in Copacabana drew approximately 8,900 people at 11:30 a.m., according to Cebrap and More in Common, with a 12-point percentage margin of error (between 7,800 and 9,900 attendees). The event, titled 'Flávio Bolsonaro: The Rescue of Brazil,' used AI-powered P2PNet technology to automatically count heads in drone-captured images, with public image access for transparency. In contrast, Lula’s (PT) campaign opening rally in São Bernardo do Campo had no public attendance measurement due to the Presidency’s denial of drone overflight permission.

item.title: Renan Santos inicia campanha com colete à prova de balas e ataques a Lula e Flávio
item.description: Renan Santos launched his presidential campaign in São Paulo, wearing a bulletproof vest during his speech at Largo São Francisco. He attacked President Lula and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, declaring that 'enemies of the nation' will be treated as enemies and described his campaign as a 'gunpowder trail' to awaken the country.

item.title: Flavio Dino publica foto na praia e diz ser imagem de 2023
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Flávio Dino dismissed allegations of improper use of an official vehicle by sharing a 2023 beach photo showing him opening the door of a private car, stressing the image is old and he was not yet a minister at the time. He condemned the spread of fake news, arguing it fuels hatred and endangers public officials, and urged journalists to correct the record in the name of ethical reporting. The controversy resurfaced amid an investigation into reports by journalist Luís Pablo, who examined the use of TJ-MA official vehicles by Dino and relatives, and had his communications’ secrecy lifted by order of Justice Alexandre de Moraes.

item.title: Zema abre campanha em Montes Claros e provoca Lula
item.description: Romeu Zema (Novo) launched his presidential campaign in Montes Claros (MG), criticizing Lula’s government and proposing 'three shocks': spending control, anti-corruption, and public security, including measures like lowering the age of criminal responsibility and building a maximum-security prison in the North. In a campaign video, he used AI and puppets to provoke Lula, depicting a paper airplane flying into Congress and landing on a Lula puppet — despite the presidential workplace being the Palácio do Planalto, not Congress.

item.title: Mário Gomes posa com Flávio Bolsonaro e pede o Exército nas ruas
item.description: Actor Mario Gomes, a federal deputy candidate, posed with Flávio Bolsonaro and advocated for military intervention in Rio de Janeiro’s streets to curb violence, referencing an armed assault on his home. He also announced an education project he intends to present to the senator, claiming Bolsonaro 'will believe in me'.

item.title: Renan Santos diz que Brasil é “nação derrotada” e promete mudança
item.description: Renan Santos, 42, businessman and co-founder of the MBL, officially launched his presidential campaign in a São Paulo rally wearing a bulletproof vest, declaring Brazil a 'defeated nation'. He promised to make Brazil one of the world's most powerful nations through a 'serious, ambitious, tough and rigid' government, emphasizing public security with war-like rhetoric and threats against criminal factions like PCC and Comando Vermelho. He stated that 'the only number that surpasses 13 is 14', seemingly referencing his electoral number or symbolically overcoming the PT (13).

item.title: Ana Estela Haddad entra na coordenação da campanha de Lula em SP
item.description: Ana Estela Haddad, Secretary of Digital Information and Health at the Ministry of Health, accepted an invitation to join the coordination of Lula's (PT) electoral campaign in São Paulo, alongside lawyer Marco Aurélio de Carvalho, founder of the Prerrogativas group. Her appointment underscores the campaign’s emphasis on digital health and information, supported by figures linked to human rights and democratic institutions.

item.title: Lula decide não ir a debate da Band e alega desigualdade de condições
item.description: President Lula's campaign announced it will not participate in the Bandeirantes TV debate scheduled for Sunday (23), citing unequal conditions to defend himself against opponents' attacks. The decision was made public on Thursday (08/16/2026) by the PT team, which argues the debate format is unfair to the incumbent candidate.

item.title: Flamengo goleia Mirassol em jogo de seis gols e se aproxima do Palmeiras na liderança do Brasileiro
item.description: Flamengo defeated Mirassol 5-1 in the 23rd round of the Brasileirão, reaching 45 points and cutting Palmeiras' lead to three points. Goals from Carrascal, Luiz Araújo, Pedro (twice) and Samuel Lino secured the win, as Flamengo capitalized on Palmeiras' loss to Fluminense and moved closer to the top, still with a postponed match against Mirassol at the Maracanã.

item.title: Cleitinho propõe reduzir isenções para enfrentar dívida de Minas
item.description: Cleitinho Azevedo, the Republican candidate for governor of Minas Gerais, proposed reducing tax exemptions to address the state's nearly R$200 billion debt, alongside spending cuts and fighting tax evasion. He also pledged to lower the IPVA from 4% to 3% and ease electricity and water bills, emphasizing the need to negotiate with the next Brazilian president regardless of who wins the 2026 election.

item.title: Tarcísio fala em “falsa comunicação” sobre PM perseguir Haddad
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas dismissed Fernando Haddad's claims of being pursued by military police, calling the account 'false communication' and stating that GPS data and camera footage showed no irregularities. The SSP-SP released a video showing a police vehicle passing Haddad's parked car without intervention, supporting the conclusion that no pursuit occurred.

item.title: Marçal diz que declaração de R$ 7,4 bilhões ao TSE está errada
item.description: Businessman Pablo Marçal (PRTB) claimed that his asset declaration of R$ 7.4 billion submitted to the TSE is incorrect and said he requested a correction. As of Sunday night, the 16th, he had not disclosed what the correct value should be. The statement was made in an interview with Estadão.

item.title: Candidatos trocam acusações em 1º debate pelo governo de Minas
item.description: In the first televised debate for the Minas Gerais gubernatorial race, candidates Cleitinho Azevedo, Alexandre Kalil, Flávio Roscoe, Gabriel Azevedo, and Mateus Simões exchanged accusations over state debt, public safety, and femicide, with heated exchanges on the Propag program and allegations of corruption and nepotism. Kalil criticized the Propag as an 'aggression against Minas,' while Cleitinho called it a 'necessary evil' and advocated for renegotiation with the federal government. PT candidate Patrus Ananias did not attend the debate.

item.title: No dia 1 de campanha, PT faz culto à personalidade de Lula e PL projeta Flávio com antipetismo
item.description: On the first day of the 2026 election campaign, the PT held a personality cult event for Lula, emphasizing his union background and seeking to reconnect with militants through the slogan 'One like you can do more'. Meanwhile, the PL projected Senator Flávio Bolsonaro as its candidate, attempting to forge an independent identity beyond being the 'son of hope', while centering its narrative on anti-PT sentiment.

item.title: Flávio assiste à derrota do Vasco, encontra Neymar e é vaiado
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, the PL party's presidential candidate, attended Vasco's loss to Santos at São Januário stadium on Sunday, following the official launch of his campaign in Copacabana. He was accompanied by Douglas Ruas, PL's candidate for Rio de Janeiro governor, and met with Neymar before the match, during which he was booed by some fans.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro vê Santos derrotar Vasco e tem camisa autografada por Neymar
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, the PL party's presidential candidate, attended a Vasco vs Santos match in the Brazilian Championship after holding an electoral rally on Copacabana Beach. He wore a Neymar-autographed jersey and showed support for Santos during the game. The event took place following his campaign debut.

item.title: Governo Trump chama de “censura” regra eleitoral brasileira para o X
item.description: U.S. Deputy Assistant Secretary for Public Diplomacy Sarah B. Rogers criticized a Brazilian electoral rule that forced X to adjust its recommendation system for the 2026 elections, calling it 'censorship imposed by Brazil'. The statement followed the platform's release of an updated algorithm to comply with local regulations.

item.title: Lula e Flávio mostram suas diferenças e duas coisas em comum no 1º dia de campanha
item.description: On the first day of the 2026 electoral campaign, Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro emphasized their differences through identity-based and legacy-driven narratives: Lula highlighted his historical ties to the working class and the PT militant base, while Flávio invoked his father Jair Bolsonaro’s legacy and the green-and-yellow symbolism seen at Copacabana. Despite the polarization, both attempted to shift toward substantive proposals for national challenges, with Lula framing his re-election bid as essential to preventing the return of Bolsonarist right-wing power, particularly citing the previous administration’s handling of the pandemic.

item.title: Eleição tem maioria de candidatos homens, brancos e empresários; veja gráficos
item.description: The 2026 Brazilian election features a majority of male candidates (65%), white candidates (48.64%), and business owners, based on TSE data updated through March 15. Women account for only 35% of candidacies, while brown and Black candidates together make up nearly 50%, despite being the majority in the electorate. The most represented age group is 45–54 years (32.52%), with candidates aged 18–24 comprising just 1.26% of total applicants.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro diz ter sido alvo de mais de 1,8 mil ameaças de morte
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) claims to have received over 1,800 death threats after proposing to classify PCC, CV, and militias as terrorist organizations, stating that 30 of those threats led to investigations by the Senate Police. He accuses the Lula government of inciting violence through remarks about 'traitors of the Fatherland' and says he dismissed Federal Police escort due to suspicions of PT-linked infiltrates.
